subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 72-year-old man with atrial fibrillation takes warfarin and presents with melena and lightheadedness. His INR is 8.4 and his hemoglobin has fallen to 8.1 g/dL. He is resuscitated with fluids and packed red cells, and he receives an intravenous dose of vitamin K together with a prothrombin complex concentrate, after which his INR falls toward the therapeutic range over the next 24 hours.
question: Warfarin produced this patient's bleeding tendency by which of the following mechanisms?

options.text: Chelation of calcium ions required for coagulation factor activity
Blockade of intestinal absorption of vitamin K
Inhibition of vitamin K epoxide reductase, preventing regeneration of reduced vitamin K
Activation of antithrombin III with inactivation of thrombin and factor Xa

explanation_correct: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), the enzyme that regenerates reduced vitamin K from vitamin K epoxide. Without reduced vitamin K, gamma-glutamyl carboxylase cannot carboxylate glutamate residues on factors II, VII, IX, and X and on proteins C and S, so the factors are secreted in an inactive form; because the vitamin also drives synthesis of the short-lived anticoagulant proteins C and S, the anticoagulant effect is delayed in onset. Vitamin K bypasses the block by replenishing reduced vitamin K.

explanation_incorrect.A: Warfarin does not inhibit carboxylase directly; it depletes the reduced vitamin K cofactor that the carboxylase requires.
explanation_incorrect.B: Warfarin is not a calcium chelator; citrate, not warfarin, produces anticoagulation by binding calcium.
explanation_incorrect.C: Warfarin does not block vitamin K absorption; it blocks recycling of the vitamin after it is used.
explanation_incorrect.E: Antithrombin activation is the mechanism of heparin and its derivatives such as fondaparinux, not of warfarin.

educationalObjective: Warfarin anticoagulates by inhibiting vitamin K epoxide reductase and thereby reducing gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors.
